name: Piyush Kaushik Bhattacharyya
summary: Computer Science graduate (KIIT University, CGPA 8.26/10) and Advanced Application Engineering Analyst at Accenture, with hands-on experience in backend development, computer vision, and machine learning across four research and engineering internships. Established real-time surveillance, drone vision, and biomedical signal analysis systems using Python, FastAPI, PyTorch, TensorFlow, and OpenCV; co-authored two peer-reviewed papers and received a Best Paper Award at NICEDT 2025.

bullets: Currently undergoing stream-specific training in application engineering, building proficiency in software development, application testing, debugging, and enterprise technologies.
Gaining hands-on experience through structured technical training, coding exercises, and application engineering projects aligned with Accenture's delivery practices.
Prototyped an edge-cloud IoT surveillance platform using FastAPI, SQLite, and PostgreSQL to process real-time drone computer vision workloads.
Deployed YOLOv8 and YOLOv10 on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano with SAHI-inspired sliced inference, improving small-object recall by 20% while maintaining 15+ FPS.
Added automated geofence detection with Shapely and GeoPandas, cutting manual verification effort by 60%.
Developed a computer vision pipeline for 50+ RTSP surveillance streams with sub-1-second processing latency.
Improved feature extraction for low light footage, reducing false alerts by 18%.
Optimized the inference pipeline to reduce incident response time by 40%.
Built a CNN BiLSTM model for ECG classification using the PhysioNet 2021 dataset, achieving 99% classification accuracy.
Reduced inference overhead through optimized preprocessing and batched signal normalization.
Benchmarked CNN, LSTM, and hybrid architectures to select the best-performing model for ECG signal classification.
Developed a Flutter authentication prototype with facial recognition login for application access control.
Integrated GPU accelerated image processing to improve authentication performance during concurrent usage.

projects.title: Krishi Sahayak
bullets: Trained a MobileNetV2 model for crop disease classification using 2,000+ real field images, achieving 98.3% accuracy.
Compressed the trained model for offline inference on low resource Android devices.
Built a multilingual Flutter interface and integrated on device prediction for use without continuous internet connectivity.

projects.title: Drone Based Surveillance System
bullets: Implemented a drone based person detection pipeline using YOLOv8 and SAHI based tiled inference for long range surveillance.
Applied tiled inference to improve detection of small objects while keeping inference suitable for real time edge deployment.
Assembled a deployment platform compatible with commercial DJI drones for field based surveillance.
